name: GO Classes Weekly Quiz 6 | Programming in C | Pointers

question.text:
After executing following lines of C code, $\textsf{&arr[1][2]}$ is same as:

int (*a)[3];
int arr[2][3];
a = arr+1;

  1. &a[0][2]

  2. (*a+2)

  3. (int *)(&arr+1)-1

  4. *(a+2)

Which of the following function declaration can be passed to the following array?

char myArray[3][4];
  1. void fun(char a[][], int size);
  2. void fun(char a[][4], int size);
  3. void fun(char [3][], int size);

  4. void fun(char [][]a, int size);

Assume starting addresses of array arrop and twoD are $1000$ and $2000$ respectively. Also, assume that addresses are of $8$ bytes and integers are of $4$ bytes.

What will be the value of $\textsf{*pp[1]}$ after the last line $\textsf{(pp++)}$ of the following program?

int main()
{
    int **pp;
    int *arrop[3];
    int twoD[3][3] = {{1,2,3}, {7,8,9}, {4,5,6}};
    pp = arrop;
    arrop[0] = (int *)(twoD+2);
    arrop[1] = (int *)(twoD+1);
    arrop[2] = (int *)(twoD);
    pp++;
}

main()
{
    char s[]= "jjtd\0abc", *p;

    for (p = s; *p; p++) 
    {
      --(*p);
    }

    printf("%s", s);
}

What will be the output of a given program?

  1. iitb abc
  2. iisc abc
  3. iisc
  4. iitb

char my_text[]= "2023 GATE";
void fun(int position)
{
    if (my_text[position] !=' ')
    {
        fun(position+1);
        printf("%c", my_text[position]);
    }
}
int main() {
    fun(0);
}

What will be the output of a given program ?

  1. $2023$
  2. $3202$
  3. $\text{ETAG} 3202$
  4. $\text{ETAG}$

What will be the output of the following program?

#include<stdio.h>
void swap(char **s1, char **s2){
    char *tmp;
    tmp=*s1;
    *s1=*s2;
    *s2=tmp;
}
int main()
{
    char *str[3]= {"orange", "apple", "pear"};
    for (int i = 0; i<2; i++)
        swap(&strs[i], &strs[i+1]);
    printf("%s %s %s", strs[0], strs[1], strs[2]);
}
  1. pear apple orange
  2. apple pear orange
  3. orange apple pear
  4. apple orange pea

What will be the output of the following program?

int main()
{
    int arr[3][3] = {{1,2,3}, {4,5,6}, {7,8,9}};
    int *p;
    p = (int *)(arr+2);
    printf("%d", *(p-2));
}

What will be the output of the following program ?

#include<stdio.h>
void fun(int c[2][2]){
    c = c+1;
    *c[1] = 5;
    (*c)[1] = 6;
}
int main()
{
    int a[3][2] = {{1,2}, {10,20}, {40, 50}};
    fun(a);
    printf("%d %d", a[2][0], a[1][0]);
}
  1. $5\; 10$
  2. $10\; 5$
  3. $10\; 40$
  4. Error since $c$ is a two-dimensional array, and we can not update the value of $c$ using $c=c+1.$

#include<stdio.h>
int bar(int data[], int i, int a, int x) {
    if (x<0) return 0;
    x--;
    int b = a + data[i];
    if(data[i] >0) return bar(data, i+1, b, x);
    if(data[i] == 0 || i ==x-1) return a;
    return -a;
}
int main()
{
    int data[5] = {1,2,3, -1};
    int x = (int *)(&data+1)-data;
    printf("%d", bar(data, 0, 0, x) );
}

What will be the output of a given program?

  1. $6$
  2. $-6$
  3. $0$
  4. $5$

What will be the output of the following program?

#include<stdio.h>
main()
{
    int a[2][3][4];
    printf("%d", a[1][0]-a[0][2]);
}

What will be the output of the following program?

main()
{
    int a[2][2] = { {1,2},{3,4} };
    int(*p)[2][2];
    p = &a;
    printf("%d", (*p)[0][0]);
}
  1. $1$
  2. $3$
  3. $4$
  4. None of these

void mystery(int n) {
  if (n <= 1) {
    printf("%d", n);
  }
  else {
    printf("%d, ", n);

    mystery(n/2);
    printf(", %d", n);
  }
}

What will be the output printed by $\text{mystery(12)}?$

  1. $12, 6, 3, 1, 3, 6, 12$
  2. $12, 6, 3, 1, 3, 6,$
  3. $12, 6, 3, 1, 3, 6, 12,$
  4. None of these

#include<stdio.h>
#include<string.h>
char upstr[50];

void putStar (int n,char str[]){
    upstr[n] = str[n];
    if(n == strlen(str))
        return;
    else upstr[n+1] = '*';
    putStar(n+1,str);
}

int main()
{
    char str[] = "hello";
    putStar (0, str);
    printf("%s", upstr); 
}

What will be the output of the given program?

  1. h*e*l*l*o
  2. h*e*l*l*o*
  3. h*e*l*l*
  4. hello

char *strcollection[3]= {"GOClasses", "GATEOverflow", "IISc"};

For the above declaration, consider base addresses of strcollection, "GOClasses", "GATEOverflow" and "IISc” are $1000, 2000, 3000$  and $4000$ respectively.

What will be value of strcollection$+1?$

Assume character is of one bytes, integer is of two bytes and address is of four bytes.

Consider the following declaration of pointer variable p.

int (*p)[10];

If the initial value of $p$ is $1100,$ then what will be the value of $\textsf{p+1}?$

It is given that, system has $8$ bytes of address size and $4$ bytes of integer size.

  1. $1140$
  2. $1180$
  3. $1104$
  4. $1108$

int mystry (char* str) {
    if (*str == 0) {
        return 0;
    }
    return mystry (str+1) +1;
}

What will be the output of mystry("hello")?

Consider the following declarations of variables in a system having $4$ bytes for integers.

int a[5][4];
int (*p1)[2];
int (*p2)[2];
int (*t1)[4];
int (*t2)[4];

Suppose array a has base address of $1000$ and initial values of $p1, p2, t1$ and $t2$ are $1000, 1048, 1016$ and $1064$ respectively. What will be the value of $p2-p1$ and $t2-t1$ respectively?

  1. $6 \;3$
  2. $48\; 24 $
  3. $12\; 6$
  4. $24\; 12$
